house_rules: Suggestions are drafts for the communications team; nothing is published automatically.
Pages listed under 'Recently changed' were just edited: don't recommend changing them again until their hold ends; judge them by the before/after numbers.
Never invent historical facts, dates, names, prices or hours. Use only what the page already says, or flag it for verification.
Never quote or paraphrase Theodore Roosevelt. Say 'consider a verified TR quote about X' instead.
Voice: friendly, plain, concrete (a knowledgeable park ranger, not a professor). Keep 'we/our/us' to a minimum.
No specific years in visitor copy; write seasons as months.
A Library visit takes about 3 1/2 hours. Never present a shorter visit as typical.
Nonpartisan: no current political figures or debates.
Page titles: the site appends ' | Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library' automatically; suggest only the page-specific part, 60 characters or fewer.
Meta descriptions: 120-155 characters with a reason to click.
Website changes are made in Drupal Layout Builder by the TRPL team; bugs and features go to the developers (FiveJars).

The Square Deal was Theodore Roosevelt's domestic policy founded on three core goals, known as the Three Cs: control of corporations, consumer protection, and conservation of natural resources. It aimed to balance the interests of workers, business owners, and consumers with the federal government acting as an honest referee.

content_additions.for_query: Can you explain Theodore Roosevelt's Square Deal domestic policy and its main goals?
content_additions.suggestion: Complete the truncated ending paragraph and add a concise summary list of goals at the end of the page to give AI answer engines clean, extractable text.
content_additions.draft:
Key Goals of the Square Deal:
- Control of Corporations: Break up abusive monopolies, regulate unfair railroad pricing, and enforce fair corporate taxation while distinguishing between good trusts and bad trusts.
- Consumer Protection: Shield public health by holding food and drug makers accountable for safe, honest goods.
- Conservation: Protect public lands, waterways, and forests for the lasting benefit of all citizens.

sitewide_issues.title: Sitewide description still says the Library is about to open
sitewide_issues.detail: Library: “Independently operated presidential library in Medora, North Dakota, dedicated to the life, legacy, and ideals of Theodore Roosevelt. Opens July 4, 2026.” · Website: “The official website of the Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library, opening July 4, 2026 in Medora, North Dakota.”
sitewide_issues.fix: Update the description in the sitewide schema (Drupal Metatag/Schema settings) to present tense, e.g. “Presidential library and museum in Medora, North Dakota, dedicated to the life, legacy, and ideals of Theodore Roosevelt. Opened July 4, 2026.” AI tools copy this sentence into answers.

sitewide_issues.title: Sitewide markup doesn't link to the Library's Wikipedia or Wikidata entry
sitewide_issues.detail: sameAs lists only social accounts. Wikipedia and Wikidata links are how search engines and AI tools confirm that trlibrary.com is the same Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library they know about.
sitewide_issues.fix: Add these to sameAs in the sitewide schema.

sitewide_issues.title: 236 pages point to a Theodore Roosevelt entity that is never defined
sitewide_issues.detail: Every /tr page says it's about https://www.trlibrary.com/tr/#person, but no page says who that is: no name, no Wikidata link. To a machine it's an empty placeholder, so the link to the real Theodore Roosevelt is lost.
sitewide_issues.fix: Define the entity once in the sitewide @graph (so every page carries it). This is the single highest-value change for the /tr section.

sitewide_issues.title: www.trlibrary.com has no llms.txt
sitewide_issues.detail: llms.txt is a plain-text guide that tells AI tools what the site covers and which pages matter. A draft built from the sitemap is attached.
sitewide_issues.fix: Review the draft, then ask FiveJars to serve it at https://www.trlibrary.com/llms.txt.

sitewide_issues.title: Restaurant and store hours are listed as the museum's hours
sitewide_issues.detail: The museum entity carries 15 hours entries, including restaurant, store hours. Machines can't tell which hours mean the museum is open.
sitewide_issues.fix: Keep only museum hours on the Library entity. Give the restaurant and the store their own entities (Restaurant, Store) with their hours, linked with containsPlace.

sitewide_issues.title: No admission information in the markup
sitewide_issues.detail: “How much are tickets?” is one of the most common visitor questions. The markup has no price or ticket link.
sitewide_issues.fix: Add admission offers (and isAccessibleForFree: false) to the Library entity.

sitewide_issues.title: 35 unaliased /node/ URLs are in the sitemap
sitewide_issues.detail: These are duplicate addresses for pages that have proper URLs (or old, unpublished-looking items). They waste crawler time and split signals between two addresses.
sitewide_issues.fix: Ask FiveJars to leave unaliased /node/ URLs out of the XML sitemap.

sitewide_issues.title: 22 pages have dates without a colon in the time zone
sitewide_issues.detail: For example datePublished “2020-10-27T06:00:00-0600” on /about/press/press-releases/trplf-announces-100-million-commitments-unlocks-50-million-state. Strict ISO 8601 wants “-06:00”, and some validators reject the short form.
sitewide_issues.fix: In the Drupal schema templates, format dateModified, datePublished, endDate, startDate with the PHP date format “c” (e.g. 2020-10-27T06:00:00-06:00).

sitewide_issues.title: 277 articles are labelled og:type “website”
sitewide_issues.detail: Social and AI previews treat them as generic pages rather than articles.
sitewide_issues.fix: Set og:type to “article” on /tr, press release and podcast templates (Drupal Metatag).

content_types.why: The /tr section is the Library's richest content for AI answers. Article markup says who published it, when it was updated, and that it's about Theodore Roosevelt (linked to his Wikidata entry).
content_types.drupal_fix: Add Article JSON-LD to the /tr article template with about = Theodore Roosevelt (the sitewide #theodore-roosevelt entity) and dateModified from the node's changed date.

acceptedAnswer.text: You can make a secure online payment through the website: trlibrary.com/donate . Or, send a check payable to the Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library Foundation to: TR Library 401 E Main Ave Ste 201 Bismarck, ND 58501.

mainEntity.name: IF I JOIN A BENEFACTOR SOCIETY, HOW WILL MY DONATION BE USED?

acceptedAnswer.text: Your donation will provide funding for physical and virtual programing and operations to explore the life, legacy, and enduring relevance of Theodore Roosevelt.

mainEntity.name: MAY I DIRECT MY GIFT TO SUPPORT A SPECIFIC AREA OF TRPL?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most powerful way to support the Library is with an unrestricted gift. Unrestricted support gives us the flexibility to direct resources where the need and opportunity are greatest — such as to the programs, conservation, and educational work that will define the Library's future — and it ensures your generosity has the broadest possible impact. That said, we're always glad to hear from benefactors with a particular passion. If you'd like to support a specific area, we welcome the conversation and would be pleased to explore opportunities that align with your interests and the Library's long-term vision. However you choose to give, your support will be recognized through the appropriate Benefactor Society.

mainEntity.name: WHAT IS THE TAX-EXEMPT STATUS OF THE THEODORE ROOSEVELT PRESIDENTIAL LIBRARY?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library Foundation manages the Library and fundraises on its behalf. The Foundation is a tax-exempt 501(c)(3) organization.

mainEntity.name: WILL MY GIFT BE TAX DEDUCTIBLE?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, gifts are 100% tax-deductible to the full extent of the law.

mainEntity.name: WILL I RECEIVE A TAX RECEIPT?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, a tax receipt will be provided.

mainEntity.name: WHAT ARE SOME OF THE BENEFACTOR SOCIETY BENEFITS?

acceptedAnswer.text: Benefits include a special welcome packet, the Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library e-newsletter and digital recognition (unless anonymity is requested). Additional opportunities for recognition are available based on level of support.

mainEntity.name: HOW LONG DOES MY BENEFACTOR SOCIETY PARTICIPATION LAST?

acceptedAnswer.text: Benefactor Society participation recognizes the total impact of your cumulative giving.

mainEntity.name: DO YOU SELL OR SHARE BENEFACTOR INFORMATION WITH THIRD PARTIES?
MAY I MAKE AN ANONYMOUS GIFT TO JOIN A BENEFACTOR SOCIETY?

acceptedAnswer.text: Certainly, simply specify your desire to remain anonymous when you make your gift and your request will be honored.

mainEntity.name: WILL MY NAME BE PRINTED IN MATERIALS OR PUBLISHED IN ANY WAY?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, digital recognition (unless anonymity is requested) and additional opportunities for recognition are available based on level of support.
